questions.q: What does Salesforce send by default when an unhandled Apex exception occurs?
options: A Slack notification
A Platform Event published automatically
An email to the org's designated Apex exception recipients, containing the stack trace, exception message, and org/user identifiers
An automatic rollback of the entire org
questions.explain: The default behavior is an email containing the exception's stack trace, message, and identifying information, with no other data included.

questions.q: Why does Salesforce's own documentation discourage relying only on unhandled-exception emails for monitoring?
options: Because exception emails require a paid add-on
Because exception emails only fire once per org, ever
Because the emails are not reliably delivered
Because they carry no structured data for trend analysis, only cover genuinely unhandled exceptions, and may land in an inbox nobody actively watches
questions.explain: Exception emails give an incomplete picture: errors already caught by your own try/catch don't trigger one, and the emails themselves offer no queryable trend data.

questions.q: What does Event Monitoring's "Apex Unexpected Exception" event type provide that the default email doesn't?
options: A durable, structured, queryable record of unhandled exceptions over time, useful for spotting trends
A WSDL describing the failure
Automatic rollback of the failed DML
Automatic retry of the failed transaction
questions.explain: Event Monitoring records unhandled exceptions in structured Event Log Files rather than one-off emails, enabling trend analysis rather than manual tallying.

questions.q: What two permissions are required to query the EventLogFile object?
options: Modify All Data and View All Users
View Event Log Files and API Enabled
Customize Application and Author Apex
Manage Users and View Setup and Configuration
questions.explain: Accessing EventLogFile data requires both the View Event Log Files permission and API Enabled.

questions.q: What are the three layers of the monitoring approach this lesson recommends combining?
options: Named Credentials, External Services, and Platform Events
Debug logs only, run manually after each deploy
Custom logging for caught errors, the built-in unhandled-exception email as a backstop, and Event Monitoring's Apex Unexpected Exception event type for durable trend data
Only Event Monitoring, since it covers every possible failure
questions.explain: Each layer catches something the others miss: custom logging catches errors you deliberately handled, the email backstops anything unhandled, and Event Monitoring gives durable, queryable trend data.
